claims.scope: A documentation-absence observation only: no retrieved ML-KEM specification or draft bounds the number of ciphertexts decapsulable under one static encapsulation key, in any of the eight deployment modes census row TASK-20260805-e6a153/census.json classifies as m_class: count_unstated, and the one normative delegation chain that names a numeric pointer (draft-ietf-tls-hybrid-design-16 Sec. 2) terminates without a value on both limbs. No attack, no cost figure, no bit figure is asserted.

quotation_integrity_check.method: Every double-quoted span (length >= 10 chars) inside finding.md's markdown tables and blockquote paragraphs was extracted programmatically and checked as a whitespace-normalized, typographic-quote-normalized substring of the concatenated source corpus (census.json, census.md, reads.md, and EV-MLKEM-d146a5.yaml parsed as YAML). Ellipsized quotations ('...') were checked by verifying each side of the ellipsis independently.
issues_found_and_corrected: R15 (ECH) row: original draft spliced two source sentences with an inserted comma and dropped the leading 'However,'; corrected to two properly closed quotations matching census.json row R15's bounding_mechanism field exactly.

R17 (LAMPS X.509) row: original draft's quote punctuation did not match the source's sentence boundary; corrected to close the quotation at the exact point census.json row R17's bounding_mechanism field does, using an internal ellipsis for the omitted middle clause.

R22 (Signal one-time prekey) caveat cell: original draft attributed the phrase 'Crystals-Kyber-1024' to the row's own derivation sentence, which actually reads 'names Kyber-1024'; corrected to quote census.json row R22's caveat field exactly, distinguishing the PQXDH spec's own parenthetical example from the row's derivation sentence.

R23 (Signal last-resort prekey) row: original draft's quote ran a comma into the source's own full-stop-outside-quote punctuation; corrected to match census.json row R23's bounding_mechanism field exactly.

The EV-MLKEM-d146a5.yaml validator full-text-search quote in finding.md Section 2: original draft added parentheses around a term list that the source does not have (and reproduces a YAML line-fold artifact -- a literal space inside 'encapsulations/ ciphertexts/uses' -- that is present in the actual parsed source string, confirmed via `python3 -c "import yaml; ..."` rather than assumed from the raw file's line wrapping); corrected to quote the parsed YAML string exactly, including that artifact.

Minor quote-punctuation-placement passes (R10, R16, R19 rows): comma/period placement relative to closing quotation marks was tightened to match the source's own logical (period/comma outside the quote) convention rather than an inserted American-style convention, for individual short listed terms and one sentence-final clause. These did not change quoted content, only punctuation style.

Editorial bold emphasis inside two direct quotations (the R13/draft-ietf-tls-hybrid-design-16 blockquote in Section 2 and the R24/CFRG-draft blockquote in Section 4) was confirmed, by checking census.json's raw string fields directly (`'**' in field` returns False for both R13 and R24's bounding_mechanism/m_derivation), to be this task's own addition rather than present in the source; both are now labelled '(bold emphasis added here; not present in census.json's plain-text field)' inline. Bold emphasis inside the Bernstein footnote-19 blockquote (Section 2) was confirmed to already exist in reads.md's own transcription and required no such label.
quotation_integrity_check.remaining_known_typographic_note: In several places this document nests quotations using single quotes ('...') where the source (after JSON-string unescaping) nests them with escaped double quotes (\"...\"), e.g. census.json row R09's 'last resort' / \"last resort\" and row R10's equivalent. This is a typographic nesting-style substitution only; the quoted words themselves are identical to the source in every such case, confirmed by direct JSON-unescaped comparison.
